profile: Instrumentation: Despite the 'Jazz' genre tag, the track is purely 8-bit/chiptune electronic music, featuring retro synthesizers, square waves, noise channel percussion, and a heavy distorted bass. Vocals: None (instrumental). Mood: Energetic, frantic, playful, retro, and cybernetic. Lyrical theme: N/A. Energy arc: Starts with a fast arpeggiated intro, drops into a heavy driving groove at 4.2s, builds complexity with melodies, drops into a sparser, pulsing bridge at 51.0s, and explodes back into high energy at 65.4s.

key_moments.what: The heavy, distorted bassline and main beat kick in after the intro.
The main high-pitched lead synth melody begins.
A breakdown/bridge section starts; the beat becomes sparser and the bass pulses differently.
The full beat and high energy return with the main melody.

fitting_styles: Fitting: Abstract geometric visualizers, rhythmic montage, pixel art/retro gaming aesthetics, cyberpunk or sci-fi narratives; these suit the frantic, electronic, 8-bit nature of the track. Clashing: Traditional band performance, rustic/acoustic aesthetics, slow romantic narratives, or lyric videos (as there are no lyrics).

song_checks.check: The picture marks the heavy bass and beat drop at 4.2s with a significant visual transition, impact, or energy increase.
A new visual element, character, or motif is introduced at 17.4s to accompany the start of the lead melody.
The visual intensity decreases or the scene changes at 51.0s to reflect the sparser breakdown section.
The video returns to high energy, fast editing, or previous intense visual motifs at 65.4s when the beat drops back in.

UN.1: The concept completely clashes with the music, such as a slow romantic drama or rustic acoustic setting.
UN.3: The concept somewhat fits the electronic nature but misses the specific frantic, retro/chiptune vibe.
UN.5: The concept perfectly matches the energetic, 8-bit/chiptune genre, using appropriate aesthetics like pixel art, cyberpunk, or frantic abstract visuals.

EM.1: The video feels slow, melancholic, or completely disconnected from the track's high energy.
EM.3: The video captures the energy but lacks the playful or frantic edge of the music.
EM.5: The video perfectly conveys the playful, frantic, and driving cybernetic mood of the track.

RH.1: The visual edits and movements ignore the fast tempo and syncopated chiptune rhythms.
RH.3: The video syncs to the main beat but misses the fast arpeggios and intricate rhythmic details.
RH.5: Visual events, cuts, and motion accents are tightly locked to the fast 8-bit percussion, bassline, and arpeggios.

ST.1: The video ignores the major structural changes, maintaining a flat visual arc.
ST.3: The video responds to some changes but misses key transitions like the breakdown at 51.0s.
ST.5: The picture clearly shifts at the intro (4.2s), melody start (17.4s), breakdown (51.0s), and the energetic return (65.4s).

VA.1: The visuals are messy, low-effort, or suffer from obvious, distracting AI artifacts and glitches.
VA.3: The visuals are competent but lack polish, cohesive color grading, or strong composition.
VA.5: High-quality rendering with clean composition, cohesive colors, and a polished look, whether pixel art, 3D, or abstract.

CR.1: A generic, uninspired audio visualizer or basic template.
CR.3: A standard retro or cyberpunk video that fits but offers no surprising or distinctive ideas.
CR.5: A highly creative and distinctive interpretation of the chiptune sound that goes beyond basic retro tropes.
